record: post-hoc ratification of the H-NULL-1 inference hierarchy
note: inference_frozen.json is NOT modified. It records what was frozen BEFORE the calibration run, including its promotion_rule refusing promotion. This file records what the operator decided AFTER seeing the calibration, and why. Both must be read together; the audit trail is the pair, not either file alone.

frozen_before_the_run.promotion_rule: cluster is NOT promoted to primary

what_the_calibration_showed.moving_block: FAILED its own pre-declared gate: 9.5% rejection rate (95% CI [0.0821,0.1079]) under N5 constant LONG and N6 constant SHORT, entirely outside the pre-declared [0.02,0.08]
what_the_calibration_showed.cluster: PASSED: 6.7% (95% CI [0.056,0.078]) under the same nulls, and PASSED at every persistence level from 0.00 to 0.90 with an INCONCLUSIVE only at persistence 1.00
what_the_calibration_showed.iid: FAILED in BOTH directions: 0.8% at persistence 0.00 and 20.2% at persistence 1.00

why_this_is_not_tuning: The selection criterion -- 'PASS iff the entire 95% CI of the rejection rate lies inside [0.02,0.08]' -- was itself pre-declared and hashed into the pre-registration before any replication ran. No block length was tuned, no cluster definition was changed, no interval was widened, no seed was re-drawn. What changed is which of three ALREADY-FROZEN candidates is named primary, decided by an already-frozen rule. That is the rule doing its job. It is nonetheless a post-hoc change to a frozen hierarchy, which is why it required ratification rather than being applied silently.
ratification_text: cluster inference = PRIMARY; iid = diagnostic; moving-block = secondary diagnostic. Do not modify these because a future result looks inconvenient.
binding_consequences: Every subsequent experiment reports the cluster statistic as its headline; iid and moving-block appear as diagnostics only.
Production MDE is 0.03462 R at 2400 bets under cluster inference, scaling as 1/sqrt(n).
An observed effect below the MDE is classified INSUFFICIENT POWER, never NO EDGE.
This hierarchy may be changed only on discovery of an actual implementation defect, which must be documented and the affected frozen experiments rerun.
